# The panel matches your editor's look

The panel that shows your tracked changes automatically picks up the same colours and style as your code editor. This means every screen inside it feels like part of the same tool, not like a separate app bolted on, and it stays easy to read no matter which look you use.

## Contents

- [What it does for you](#what-it-does-for-you)
- [How it works](#how-it-works)
- [Good to know](#good-to-know)

## What it does for you

- Every part of the panel uses the same colours, so moving between screens feels consistent rather than jarring.
- It automatically matches whichever colour theme you already use in your editor, light, dark, or high contrast, with nothing for you to set up.
- Secondary or less important text stays clear and readable on both light and dark backgrounds.
- The panel looks finished and deliberate, with consistent icons, spacing, and rounded corners, instead of looking like a rough, unstyled add-on.

## How it works

1. You open the panel inside your editor.
2. The panel checks which colour theme your editor is currently using.
3. It chooses matching colours for backgrounds, borders, cards, and text based on that theme.
4. Every screen and every card in the panel picks up those colours automatically.
5. If you change your editor's theme, the panel updates its look to match.

## Good to know

- If you use a high contrast theme for accessibility reasons, the panel keeps your editor's own colours instead of applying its own style.
- There is nothing to configure, the matching happens by itself.
